_about: Rules for tools/spec_index.py and tools/spec_rules_view.py (docs/plan_model_ergonomics.md, Parts B and C). Editorial content, so it lives here and not in the tools (global rule 9). Each list says which tool reads it.

source_id_patterns._read_by: tools/spec_index.py: the citation forms of the six corpus sources and the cross-source resolutions, from docs/model_explainer.md's 'Reading the citations' table, plus the ledger's consolidated entries and the design-lessons notes. A requirement's `sources` field holds every match in its block, in order of first appearance. Finding-level forms come first, so a chapter-level form never splits one (FE03.6 is FE03.6, not FE03).

history_phrases._read_by: tools/spec_rules_view.py (C4): a sentence in a requirement body that matches one of these is an inline revision narrative, listed in docs/spec_rules/history_in_body.md for the owner's decision (Part E). The tool strips nothing. `Revision \d+` is matched as written, capitalised; a lower-case `revision N` counts only after a preposition (`corrected at revision 7`, `superseded in part at revision 14`), because a bare `(revision 22)` is a cross-reference (review 2026-10-22). The list over-includes by design: `previously` and `was changed` are rule text in some bodies, which the owner's pass will leave as they are. Extended 2026-10-22 (TODO: narrative the phrases missed): `earlier form`, `The text it replaces`, `is replaced`, `The form approved at`, `It replaces`, `As first built`, `revision N removed`, `rev-N form`.

extraction_sources._read_by: tools/spec_index.py (ledger_index): the per-finding extraction files behind the ledger's consolidated entries, indexed one record per `## … <ID> —` heading (the plan's §11 trial, 2026-10-22: a lookup of what FE03.6 says could not reach it from _LEDGER.md alone). Globs are repo-relative; files whose names start with `_` are summaries or pass notes, not entries, except the lectures file named here. The entry ID forms are the finding-level forms of source_id_patterns.
